key_insight: BudgetMem lets an LLM agent decide at runtime which memory items to use or store by routing queries through cost-aware memory tiers, preserving query-critical information while explicitly controlling latency/cost trade-offs.
problem_solved: Addresses inefficient, offline and query-agnostic memory construction for LLM agents that can discard information important to specific queries and lacks explicit control over runtime cost vs. performance.
method: Introduce a budget-tier routing architecture that partitions memory into cost/latency tiers (e.g., short-term, mid-term, long-term) and dynamically routes queries to the appropriate tier.
Use a lightweight query-aware scoring/policy module at runtime to assess informativeness and retrieval/storage value for each memory item under current budget constraints.
Enforce an explicit budget controller that allocates retrieval/storage effort per query, providing a tunable knob for the performance–cost trade-off without heavy offline preprocessing.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to deploy memory-augmented LLM agents that retain query-relevant context while meeting latency and compute budgets; useful for production systems requiring predictable cost and flexible accuracy. It enables fine-grained control over memory use and reduces waste from blanket offline memory construction.
visual_elements: Schematic pipeline: query → lightweight scorer → budget-tier router → selected memory tier → LLM, showing decision flow
Tiered memory diagram: icons for short/mid/long-term tiers annotated with cost/latency and example items
Trade-off chart: curve or cost vs. task performance with a slider illustrating the budget knob shifting operating points
Sequence example: before/after query where BudgetMem keeps a small critical memory item that offline methods would drop
paper_title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Tao Feng, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao
